stem: A web performance study measures the response time (ms) for a sample of 25 website users. The sample mean is 128.3 ms with a sample standard deviation of 38.7 ms. However, 3 of the 25 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 22 observations have a mean of 125.2 ms and standard deviation of 24.8 ms. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 128.3, 95% CI = [112.3, 144.3]. Without outliers: mean = 125.2, 95% CI = [114.6, 135.8]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [112.3, 144.3]. Point estimate: 126.8 ms.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [112.3, 144.3].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
